in_hebrew.name: בורג'ה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם בורג'ה יורד מן הספרדית, שפה רומאנסית, ממקור ערבי (בּורְג'ה) שבעצמה מתפתחת מהפרסית (בּורְג, עגוגונ) – “כביר, חזק, גדול”. השם נפוץ בקרב העם הספרדי-יהודי, והוא תועד כבר בעת העתיקה. בשפה העברית, השם בורג'ה “מקור”,  “חזק, יפה”,  ונבחר לציון חזק לב האדם, ולב שלמים.

in_latin.name: Borja
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Borja derivatur a lingua Hispanica, quae sua origine ex lingua Arabica (Burjá) proficiscitur, ipsa lingua Arabica ex lingua Persica (Burg, örigo) nata. à sua tempestate, nomen Borja in populo Iudaeorum a nobilitate Hispanica factum est. In lingua Latina, nomen Borja “nomen”, “fortis, robur, nobilis”, et ad significationem “fortis, robustus, grandis” attributum est.

in_english.name: Borja
in_english.meaning: Spanish name, strong, powerful, noble, of Spanish origin
in_english.long_meaning: The name Borja is of Spanish origin, derived from the Arabic (Burjá) and ultimately from the Persian (Burg, örigo) word for “strong, powerful, grand”. In the Christian tradition, the name Borja was chosen to signify strength of heart and a perfect will. In English, the name Borja is often associated with nobility and power, reflecting the name’s rich history and cultural significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Borja has a rich cultural history, especially in Spain. Borjas were historically rulers or revolutionaries who lived in fortified enclaves, as implied by the name's origins. Several notable individuals bearing this name have shaped history, such as Francisco Borja, the founder of the Laica Society of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Mercy, and the Borja family of medieval Aragon, known for its political and military prominence.

As indicated by its etymological meaning, Borja represents a strong, fortified foundation, providing spiritual sanctuary and a secure base for personal growth and development in the face of life's challenges. Furthermore, its association with the knightly tradition and notoriety for standing up against injustice can serve as a reminder for its bearers to be steadfast in their commitment to faith and maintaining the moral high ground.
